title: Worth the Wait
description: Booking a shipment should eventually produce a notification, but not necessarily inside the same request that created it — SwiftCargo enqueues delivery on a delay. Prove the timing, not just the eventual outcome.
successCondition: Book a shipment as a customer, then immediately (within roughly 100ms) call GET /api/notifications — the notifications array does not yet contain a shipment.booked entry for this action. Poll again after waiting past the configured queue delay (NOTIFICATION_QUEUE_DELAY_MS, default 500ms) — now the notifications array contains an entry with type "shipment.booked" and unreadCount has increased by at least 1.
hints: docs/api/notifications.md is explicit that a test checking immediately and finding nothing yet is not broken — that immediate-empty result is itself part of what you're proving here, not a bug in your test.
Give yourself comfortable margin past the default 500ms delay (e.g. wait 800ms-1s) to avoid flaky timing right at the boundary.
